propositions: Completion verification currently materializes the full ticket store despite reading only a small subset, consuming 135–235 seconds on close traces; lazy pinned reads at tickets_oid with batched cat-file reduce per-ticket latency to ~29 ms.

The close path publishes PASS COMPLETION_VERDICT, STATUS transition, and completion SIGNATURE through separate writes, allowing a durable PASS to outlive a failed close and a closed ticket to outlive a failed signature; one atomic transaction must contain all three or none.

A pinned-ticket reader must resolve aliases and Jira bindings at a fixed tickets_oid snapshot without fallback to live state or caching inside the view, recording negative reads and consulted reachability in a stable receipt.

Before mutation, validate the receipt against current descendant state, reject non-ancestor history, diff changed paths, recompute affected predicates, and discard the verdict on exact/hierarchy/link/negative/resolver conflicts.

LLM work, lazy reads, receipt validation, and bundle preparation occur outside the write lock; only final HEAD/status assertions, ordering, signing, staging, and one local commit occur inside the lock.

A successful close creates exactly one local commit binding PASS COMPLETION_VERDICT, closed STATUS, and completion SIGNATURE to a single (run_id, code_oid, tickets_oid, receipt_digest) identity; any lock/staging/commit fault rolls back without leaving artifacts.
